name: Hume City Council — Data Centre Assessment Framework
approval_body: Hume City Council (Hume Planning Scheme)
notes: On 25 Aug 2025 Hume became the FIRST Victorian council to endorse a motion to develop a draft policy framework assessing data-centre applications against SUSTAINABLE RESOURCE USE, and to call on the Victorian Government to strengthen planning controls. Trigger: a 'tidal wave' of applications — ~7 data centres incoming to Hume plus 20-30 across Melbourne's west, several fast-tracked at ministerial level or surfaced only via FOI; NEXTDC Tullamarine (Sharps Road) already causing parking/amenity strain. Water pressure: Yarra Valley Water received 7 applications to draw municipal water for cooling; one approved at up to 3.94 million m3/yr (~a town of 66,000), a second approved, five under consideration. FRAMEWORK APPROACH / gaps it targets: data centres of 100-500MW+ are a new industrial land use with no policy to coordinate clusters; it seeks cumulative-impact assessment across precincts, a water-source hierarchy (recycled before potable), Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) reporting, and early council involvement rather than ministerial bypass. Names the core cooling trade-off: evaporative (water-heavy) cooling uses 20-30% less electricity than dry cooling, so high power prices push developers toward water. Sits in tension with the state's $5.5M Sustainable DC Action Plan (aiming to unlock ~$25bn capex). Cr Jim Kurt lead ('a wicked problem... huge in scale, consuming massive amounts of water and electricity whilst offering little back... in terms of jobs'). To read: Star Weekly (source), ABC News 26 Aug 2025, TBH Consultancy 'Rethinking Water and Data Centre Growth in Melbourne', Concerned Waterways Alliance, Planning Institute 'Planning for Data Centres' guidance note.

name: Hume City Council — data centre moratorium motion (Aug 2026)
notes: On 10 Aug 2026, following an earlier report of 23 Feb 2026, Hume City Council moved to write to the Premier, the Minister for Planning, the Minister for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Economy and the Minister for Jobs, Industry and Advanced Manufacturing seeking a MORATORIUM on approvals for new data centres and expansions of existing data centres until a Victorian Parliamentary Joint Select Committee Inquiry into Data Centres is completed, with public hearings and evidence from scientific experts, community organisations, Traditional Owners, residents, local government, industry and agencies. This is the strongest local-government position recorded so far and sits alongside the City of Whittlesea resolution of 18 Aug 2026 (inquiry, taskforce, publish the Sustainable Data Centre Action Plan) and the City of Melbourne draft position paper of Aug 2026. Source: City of Whittlesea report to Council 18 Aug 2026, agenda item 5.1. See also the existing row 'Hume City Council — Data Centre Assessment Framework'.

name: Western Australia — data centres undefined in planning schemes
notes: Structural governance gap, reported 13 Aug 2026. Data centres are not a defined land use in WA planning schemes, so councils must classify them as 'warehouse' or 'industrial', or else as a 'use not listed' — which makes them potentially approvable in ANY zone. Planning lawyer Belinda Moharich and City of Gosnells Mayor Terresa Lynes both state that councils have asked for state government leadership on data centre regulation and none has been offered. A City of Stirling motion to ban data centres failed 4 votes to 8 on 13 Aug 2026. Concerns raised: cooling water use, noise from fans and backup diesel generators, air quality from generators, and broader public health impacts. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE MAP: WA sits outside the Planning Pathway vocabulary the tracker uses elsewhere — there is no state fast-track to record because there is no state framework at all. 'Local council' is set as the pathway because that is where these decisions land by default, not because WA has chosen a council-led model. Governance Flags left unset: the deficit here is an absence of category, which none of the three existing flag options describes. Contrast NSW (17 Aug framework), VIC (DFP) and QLD (counter-proposal).
